function.name: Product Management
function.label: Product Management Function
function.essence: Product Management governs what the product is and why, from market, user, and business inputs.
function.dek: A governed system of activities, capabilities, and tools — this is a function model, not a process nor a lifecycle — inputs to outputs.

capabilities.note: Analyzing competitors, markets and tradeoffs to find where the product wins: cheaper, faster, higher quality.

blocks.text: Most experienced product executives can feel when product management is working and when it's fragmented. It can be difficult to articulate why. The usual answers reach for process maturity or tooling — which is an overcomplication.
PMs are taught sprints, ceremonies, and cadences without knowing the layer beneath. They get the verbs without the nouns.
The product management function can be represented at three levels, and each answers a different question:

items.text: flat and structural. What must exist: inputs, activities, capabilities, outputs. No sequence, no arrows. A trigger presumes a time axis, and this layer has none.
a linear path through part of the function. The function model is the dictionary; a process is a sentence built from it.
the function projected onto time, derived from the processes that form the flywheel of a practice.

blocks.text: Most organizations struggle to adopt lifecycles before they understand the function.

items.text: is a flat, ontological form; what the function is and what it does.
are linear renderings of portions of the function.
is an approximate rendering of the function in motion. That's what it looks like when it's running.

blocks.text: This page represents the first layer only. Nothing here is missing an arrow. Arrows belong to a different diagram, answering a different question.

function.name: Product Marketing
function.label: Product Marketing Function
function.essence: Product Marketing governs product meaning at the enterprise boundary.
function.dek: A bounded corollary to the Product Management function — focused on market translation, launch communication, and field enablement.

function.name: Software Engineering

function.essence: Software Engineering governs how the product is built: reliable, secure, maintainable software that meets requirements and can evolve.
function.dek: Transforms approved requirements into reliable, secure, maintainable software that delivers value in production.
